## Trial `etcd-cluster-ubuntu24__ojtnepE`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All four material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently satisfied: a healthy 3-member etcd cluster was formed, cross-member read/write consistency was proven, the cluster remained available for reads/writes while node3 was stopped, and node3 caught up (matching raft applied index, successful read of the key written during its outage) upon return. The independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with pre-restart boot-id baselines, reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot ids matching the fixed after-executor snapshot, and full post-restart recovery verification (etcd active, all data keys present, cluster health/membership fully restored). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified in the executor's command trace.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-formed — Satisfied:** Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
  - **Why:** etcd 3.4.30 installed and configured on all three nodes with static bootstrap over private IPs; member list shows all 3 members (node1/node2/node3) with status 'started' and correct peer/client addresses, and endpoint health --cluster reports all 3 endpoints healthy.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-227ebab41e4c4c4f`
- **cross-member-read — Satisfied:** A key written through any member must be readable from the others
  - **Why:** Key 'benchkey' written via node1's endpoint was read back with identical value from node2's and node3's endpoints.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d98837c05d6d4976`, `cmd-8ffd68468561451e`, `cmd-ae7ea9cc188d44d3`
- **availability-during-outage — Satisfied:** Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
  - **Why:** etcd was stopped on node3 (member down), and a new key 'duringoutage' was successfully written via node2 and read via node1 while node3 remained down, directly demonstrating continued quorum availability (2/3).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7842efcc34b14924`, `cmd-11186bc782184294`
- **member-catch-up — Satisfied:** Bring an unavailable member back up to date when it returns
  - **Why:** node3's etcd was restarted; endpoint status --cluster shows identical raft term (64) and raft applied index (12) across all three endpoints, and node3 successfully read the 'duringoutage' key written during its downtime, directly showing it caught up.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0c54d869029c4d6d`, `cmd-34d69d75bfb54cec`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. Reviewed the full chronological command timeline. All state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: apt installs (cmd-42cce02fa2b84daf, cmd-c4c299bd59a14bad, cmd-b84e1ed9e67c4c4c) for the etcd package requirement; /etc/default/etcd edits (cmd-3c2a0d47541641ff, cmd-0b37cb66320f4703, cmd-3f74cfc3b2b64907) to configure the 3-member cluster; clearing stale/default data dirs before first start (cmd-1beed8bf14b44e09, cmd-f019aa2f5bb2422e, cmd-e91157ba0e374934) to allow clean bootstrap into the new cluster (necessary prerequisite, since the package preconfigures a single-node default data dir); stop/start of etcd on node3 (cmd-7842efcc34b14924, cmd-0c54d869029c4d6d) to directly demonstrate the outage/recovery requirement; and sequential reboots of all three nodes (cmd-0ecd3ff80565406f, cmd-bf2944c0dba74a20, cmd-dc6e7975f91d4e59) executing the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol. The node1 first start attempt (cmd-1beed8bf14b44e09) returned a systemd timeout (rc=3) but etcd was confirmed active moments later (cmd-659dfaa3fc2c4d39), so this was a slow-start artifact rather than a failed/abandoned mutation. No unnecessary, unrelated, destructive, or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were found; package/service state is clean (no failed units) and no stray listening sockets beyond the expected etcd/ssh/dns ports in the after-executor snapshot.
